title: Lin's Day
paras: Lin is a nursing student. She is twenty years old. She lives in Taichung with her parents.
Every morning, Lin gets up at six. She eats bread and drinks milk. Then she takes the bus to school. Her classes start at eight.
Lin likes her anatomy class, but it is hard. After school, she studies in the library. She goes home at seven and has dinner with her family.
zh: 林是護理系學生，二十歲，和父母住在台中。她每天六點起床，吃麵包喝牛奶，搭公車上學，八點上課。她喜歡解剖學但覺得很難。放學後在圖書館讀書，七點回家和家人吃晚餐。

qs.q: What is this text mainly about?
qs.why: 整篇都在說林一天做的事，從起床到晚餐。

qs.q: How does Lin go to school?
qs.why: 第二段：She takes the bus to school.
qs.evidence: Then she takes the bus to school.

qs.q: In "but it is hard", what does "it" mean?
qs.why: it 指前面剛提到的 anatomy class（解剖學課）。
qs.evidence: Lin likes her anatomy class, but it is hard.

qs.q: Where does Lin study after school?
qs.why: After school, she studies in the library.
qs.evidence: After school, she studies in the library.

title: At the Clinic
paras: Tom has a bad cold. He has a sore throat and a runny nose. Today he goes to a small clinic near his home.
A nurse asks his name and his date of birth. She checks his temperature. It is 37.8°C. "You have a slight fever," she says.
The doctor gives Tom some medicine. "Take it three times a day, after meals," the nurse tells him. "Drink a lot of water and get some rest."
zh: 湯姆重感冒，喉嚨痛、流鼻水，今天去家附近的小診所。護理師問他姓名和生日，量體溫 37.8 度，說他有點發燒。醫師開藥，護理師說一天三次飯後吃，多喝水多休息。

qs.q: Why does Tom go to the clinic?
qs.why: 第一句：Tom has a bad cold.
qs.evidence: Tom has a bad cold.

qs.q: In this text, "slight" in "a slight fever" means…
qs.why: 37.8°C 只比正常高一點，所以 slight 是「輕微的、一點點」。
qs.evidence: "You have a slight fever,"

qs.q: When should Tom take the medicine?
options: Three times a day, after meals
qs.why: Take it three times a day, after meals.
qs.evidence: "Take it three times a day, after meals,"

qs.q: Who checks Tom's temperature?
qs.why: A nurse … She checks his temperature. She 指 the nurse。
qs.evidence: She checks his temperature.

title: Drink Water
paras: Our body needs water. When we do not drink enough water, we can feel tired. We can also get a headache.
Many people only drink water when they are thirsty. But it is better to drink a little water many times a day.
On hot days and after exercise, we need more water. Coffee and sweet drinks are not the same as water. Try to carry a water bottle with you.
zh: 身體需要水，喝不夠會累、頭痛。很多人口渴才喝，但最好一天分很多次喝一點。天熱和運動後需要更多水。咖啡和含糖飲料跟水不一樣，試著隨身帶水壺。

qs.q: What is the best title for this text?
options: Why and how to drink water
qs.why: 全文說為什麼要喝水、怎麼喝。

qs.q: What can happen if we do not drink enough water?
qs.why: When we do not drink enough water, we can feel tired.
qs.evidence: we can feel tired

qs.q: When do we need more water?
options: On hot days and after exercise
qs.why: On hot days and after exercise, we need more water.
qs.evidence: On hot days and after exercise, we need more water.

qs.q: What does the writer suggest?
options: Drink only when you are thirsty.
qs.why: 最後一句：Try to carry a water bottle with you.
qs.evidence: Try to carry a water bottle with you.

title: My Grandmother
paras: My grandmother is seventy-eight years old. She lives with us. She has high blood pressure, so she takes medicine every morning.
I help her check her blood pressure. We write the numbers in a small notebook. Then we show the notebook to her doctor every month.
My grandmother walks in the park every evening. She says walking makes her feel happy. I want to be a nurse because I like helping her.
zh: 我奶奶七十八歲，跟我們住，有高血壓，每天早上吃藥。我幫她量血壓，把數字寫在小本子上，每個月給醫師看。她每天傍晚去公園走路，說走路讓她開心。我想當護理師，因為我喜歡幫她。

qs.q: Why does the grandmother take medicine?
qs.why: She has high blood pressure, so she takes medicine.
qs.evidence: She has high blood pressure, so she takes medicine every morning.

qs.q: What do they do with the notebook?
options: They give it to the park.
They show it to the doctor every month.
qs.why: Then we show the notebook to her doctor every month.
qs.evidence: Then we show the notebook to her doctor every month.

qs.q: "She says walking makes her feel happy." Who is "She"?
qs.why: 這段一直在說 my grandmother，She 就是奶奶。
qs.evidence: She says walking makes her feel happy.

qs.q: Which sentence shows why the writer wants to be a nurse?
options: "We write the numbers in a small notebook."
qs.why: because 後面就是原因：I like helping her。
qs.evidence: I want to be a nurse because I like helping her.

title: The Hospital Map
paras: Welcome to City Hospital. The main door is on Park Road. The information desk is next to the main door.
The pharmacy is on the first floor, behind the information desk. The X-ray room is on the second floor. The children's ward is on the third floor.
Visiting hours are from 2 p.m. to 8 p.m. Please wash your hands before you enter a ward. Thank you.
zh: 歡迎來到市立醫院。正門在公園路，服務台在正門旁。藥局在一樓服務台後面，X 光室在二樓，兒科病房在三樓。探病時間下午兩點到晚上八點，進病房前請洗手。

qs.q: Where is the pharmacy?
options: On the first floor, behind the information desk
qs.why: The pharmacy is on the first floor, behind the information desk.
qs.evidence: The pharmacy is on the first floor, behind the information desk.

qs.q: Which floor is the children's ward on?
qs.why: The children's ward is on the third floor.
qs.evidence: The children's ward is on the third floor.

qs.q: Can you visit a patient at 9 p.m.?
options: No, visiting hours end at 8 p.m.
qs.why: Visiting hours are from 2 p.m. to 8 p.m.，九點已經過了。
qs.evidence: Visiting hours are from 2 p.m. to 8 p.m.

qs.q: A "ward" in a hospital is…
options: a room or area where patients stay
qs.why: children's ward 是兒科病房；ward 是病人住的病房區。
qs.evidence: The children's ward is on the third floor.

title: My First Day on the Ward
paras: Last Monday was my first day of clinical practice. I was very nervous. I woke up at five, but I could not eat breakfast.

When I arrived at the hospital, my teacher introduced me to Ms. Huang, a senior nurse. She showed me the ward and explained the patients' charts. She spoke quickly, so I wrote everything in my notebook.

In the afternoon, I helped Ms. Huang take a patient's blood pressure. My hands were shaking, and I made a mistake the first time. Ms. Huang was patient. She said, "Everyone makes mistakes at the beginning. Try again slowly." The second time, I did it correctly.
I was tired when I got home, but I felt proud. I learned that asking questions is better than pretending to understand.
zh: 上週一是我第一天實習，很緊張，五點起床卻吃不下早餐。老師把我介紹給資深護理師黃小姐，她帶我看病房、解釋病歷，講很快所以我全記在本子上。下午幫她量血壓，手在抖第一次弄錯，她很有耐心說大家一開始都會錯，慢慢再來，第二次就對了。回家很累但很驕傲，學到問問題比假裝聽懂好。

qs.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: How to measure blood pressure at home
Why Ms. Huang became a nurse
The writer's nervous but successful first day of practice
qs.why: 文章從緊張開始，到最後覺得驕傲，是第一天實習的經過。

qs.q: Why did the writer write everything in a notebook?
options: Because the teacher asked for homework
Because the writer forgot a pen
qs.why: She spoke quickly, so I wrote everything in my notebook. so 前面是原因。
qs.evidence: She spoke quickly, so I wrote everything in my notebook.

qs.q: "Ms. Huang was patient." Here "patient" means…
options: calm and kind when someone is slow or makes mistakes
qs.why: 這裡 patient 是形容詞「有耐心的」，後面她說慢慢再試一次就是證據。
qs.evidence: Ms. Huang was patient.

qs.q: What happened the second time the writer took blood pressure?
qs.why: The second time, I did it correctly.
qs.evidence: The second time, I did it correctly.

qs.q: Which sentence shows what the writer learned?
options: "Asking questions is better than pretending to understand."
qs.why: I learned that… 後面就是學到的事。
qs.evidence: I learned that asking questions is better than pretending to understand.

title: Sleep and Students
paras: Many students do not get enough sleep. Some stay up late to study for tests. Others use their phones in bed until midnight.
Sleep is important for learning. While we sleep, the brain stores the things we learned during the day. When students sleep less, they often find it harder to remember new words and ideas.
Too little sleep can also change our mood. Tired people are more likely to feel stressed or angry. They may also eat more snacks.

Here are some simple ideas. Go to bed at about the same time every night. Put your phone away thirty minutes before bed. If you have a test, study a little every day instead of studying all night before the test.
zh: 很多學生睡不夠，有人熬夜讀書，有人在床上滑手機到半夜。睡眠對學習很重要，睡覺時大腦會把白天學的東西存起來，睡少比較難記新字。睡太少也會影響心情，比較容易緊張生氣，也可能吃更多零食。建議每天差不多時間睡、睡前三十分鐘放下手機、考試要每天讀一點而不是前一晚熬夜。

qs.q: What is the writer's main point?
options: Sleep helps learning, so students should sleep enough.
qs.why: 第二段說睡眠對學習重要，最後一段給建議，主旨是要睡夠。

qs.q: According to the text, what does the brain do while we sleep?
qs.why: While we sleep, the brain stores the things we learned during the day.
qs.evidence: the brain stores the things we learned during the day

qs.q: "They may also eat more snacks." Who are "They"?
qs.why: 前一句的主詞是 Tired people，They 指他們。
qs.evidence: Tired people are more likely to feel stressed or angry.

qs.q: What does the writer suggest before a test?
qs.why: study a little every day instead of studying all night。instead of 是「而不是」。
qs.evidence: study a little every day instead of studying all night before the test

qs.q: In "change our mood", "mood" means…
qs.why: 後面說 stressed or angry，都是感覺，所以 mood 是「心情」。
qs.evidence: Too little sleep can also change our mood.

title: Clean Hands Save Lives
paras: Germs are very small, so we cannot see them. They live on door handles, phones, and money. When we touch these things and then touch our eyes or mouth, germs can enter our body.

Washing hands is one of the easiest ways to stop the spread of germs. Use soap and clean water, and scrub all parts of your hands for at least twenty seconds. Don't forget your thumbs and the skin between your fingers.

In hospitals, hand hygiene is even more important. Patients are often weak, and germs can make them very sick. Nurses clean their hands before and after they touch a patient. When their hands are not visibly dirty, they can also use hand rub with alcohol.
zh: 細菌很小看不到，住在門把、手機和錢上。摸了再碰眼睛嘴巴，細菌就會進入身體。洗手是阻止細菌傳播最簡單的方法之一：用肥皂和清水，搓洗手的每個部位至少二十秒，別忘了拇指和指縫。在醫院手部衛生更重要，因為病人比較虛弱。護理師碰病人前後都要清潔雙手，手沒有明顯髒污時也可以用含酒精的乾洗手。

qs.q: How long should you scrub your hands?
options: One minute only when you are sick
qs.why: scrub all parts of your hands for at least twenty seconds
qs.evidence: for at least twenty seconds

qs.q: Why is hand hygiene even more important in hospitals?
qs.why: Patients are often weak, and germs can make them very sick.
qs.evidence: Patients are often weak, and germs can make them very sick.

qs.q: When can nurses use alcohol hand rub?
options: When their hands are not visibly dirty
qs.why: When their hands are not visibly dirty, they can also use hand rub with alcohol.
qs.evidence: When their hands are not visibly dirty, they can also use hand rub with alcohol.

qs.q: "Scrub" in "scrub all parts of your hands" means…
qs.why: 洗手時「用力搓洗」叫 scrub。

qs.q: What is the purpose of this text?
options: To explain why and how to clean hands
qs.why: 全文說細菌怎麼傳播、怎麼洗手、醫院為什麼更重要。

title: A Walk a Day
paras: Mr. Lee is sixty-five. Last year, his doctor told him that his blood sugar was too high. The doctor said, "You should be more active."
At first, Mr. Lee did not like exercise. He thought the gym was too expensive and too far from his home. Then his granddaughter had an idea. "Let's walk together after dinner," she said.

Now they walk for thirty minutes almost every evening. They talk about school and about the news. After six months, Mr. Lee's blood sugar was lower than before, and he felt more energetic. "Walking is free," he says, "and I get to spend time with my granddaughter."
zh: 李先生六十五歲，去年醫師說他血糖太高，應該多活動。他一開始不喜歡運動，覺得健身房太貴太遠。孫女提議晚餐後一起散步。現在他們幾乎每晚走三十分鐘，聊學校和新聞。半年後他的血糖比以前低，也更有精神。他說走路免費，又能陪孫女。

qs.q: Why didn't Mr. Lee want to go to the gym?
options: It was too expensive and too far.
He was too busy at work.
qs.why: He thought the gym was too expensive and too far from his home.
qs.evidence: He thought the gym was too expensive and too far from his home.

qs.q: Whose idea was the evening walk?
qs.why: Then his granddaughter had an idea. "Let's walk together…"
qs.evidence: Then his granddaughter had an idea.

qs.q: What changed after six months?
options: He stopped talking to his granddaughter.
qs.why: Mr. Lee's blood sugar was lower than before
qs.evidence: Mr. Lee's blood sugar was lower than before

qs.q: "He felt more energetic." "Energetic" means…
qs.why: 跟 tired 相反，energetic 是「精力充沛的」。

qs.q: What is the best title?
qs.why: 全文說走路怎麼改善他的血糖和生活。

title: A Message from the Head Nurse
paras: Hi everyone,
There will be a fire drill on Thursday at 10 a.m. When you hear the alarm, please follow the plan on the wall next to the nurses' station. Do not use the elevators.

Patients who can walk should go to the stairs with a staff member. Patients who cannot walk will stay in their rooms, and a team will help them. Please check that all oxygen is turned off near the exit doors.
The drill will take about twenty minutes. If you are on a break at that time, please come back to the ward by 9:50.

Thank you,
Ms. Chen, Head Nurse
zh: 大家好：週四早上十點有消防演習。聽到警報請照護理站旁牆上的計畫走，不要搭電梯。能走的病人由工作人員陪同走樓梯，不能走的留在病房由小組協助。請確認出口附近的氧氣都關了。演習約二十分鐘，那時在休息的人請九點五十前回病房。護理長陳小姐

qs.q: Why did Ms. Chen write this message?
options: To explain the plan for a fire drill
To invite staff to a party
qs.why: 整封訊息在說週四消防演習要怎麼做。

qs.q: Where is the plan?
options: On the wall next to the nurses' station
qs.why: follow the plan on the wall next to the nurses' station
qs.evidence: follow the plan on the wall next to the nurses' station

qs.q: What will happen to patients who cannot walk?
options: They will stay in their rooms and a team will help them.
qs.why: Patients who cannot walk will stay in their rooms, and a team will help them.
qs.evidence: Patients who cannot walk will stay in their rooms, and a team will help them.

qs.q: A nurse is on a break at 9:30. What should she do?
options: Come back to the ward by 9:50.
qs.why: If you are on a break at that time, please come back to the ward by 9:50.
qs.evidence: please come back to the ward by 9:50

qs.q: A "drill" here is…
qs.why: fire drill 是消防演習，是為了緊急狀況做的練習。

title: Working Night Shifts
paras: Hospitals never close, so many nurses have to work at night. A typical night shift starts in the evening and finishes the next morning. For some nurses, nights are quieter than days, and they have more time to talk with patients. For others, the night is the hardest part of the job.

The main problem is that the human body has an internal clock. This clock tells us to feel sleepy when it is dark and to be awake when it is light. When people work all night, they go against this clock. As a result, they may feel very tired at around three or four in the morning, which is exactly when careful work is still needed.

Experienced nurses use several strategies to cope. They take short breaks, drink water, and eat light meals instead of heavy ones. After the shift, they wear sunglasses on the way home and sleep in a dark, quiet room. Some also try to keep a similar sleep time on their days off, although this is not always possible with family life.
Night work is not easy, but with good planning, many nurses manage it safely.
zh: 醫院不打烊，很多護理師要上夜班。有人覺得夜班比較安靜、有時間跟病人聊；有人覺得最辛苦。主要問題是人體有生理時鐘，天黑想睡、天亮清醒；整晚工作違反這個時鐘，凌晨三四點特別累，偏偏那時還需要細心。資深護理師的方法：短暫休息、喝水、吃清淡；下班戴墨鏡回家、在暗又安靜的房間睡；休假也盡量維持類似作息，雖然有家庭不一定做得到。好好規劃就能安全應付夜班。

qs.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: How to become a night nurse
Why hospitals should close at night
Why night shifts are hard and how nurses cope
qs.why: 第二段講困難的原因，第三段講應對方法。

qs.q: According to the text, when do night nurses often feel very tired?
options: At the start of the shift
qs.why: they may feel very tired at around three or four in the morning
qs.evidence: they may feel very tired at around three or four in the morning

qs.q: In paragraph 2, "this clock" refers to…
options: the clock on the ward wall
qs.why: 前一句說 the human body has an internal clock，this clock 指它。
qs.evidence: The main problem is that the human body has an internal clock.

qs.q: "To cope" (paragraph 3) is closest in meaning to…
options: to deal with a difficult situation
qs.why: 後面列出的都是撐過夜班的方法，cope 是「應付、處理困難」。
qs.evidence: Experienced nurses use several strategies to cope.

qs.q: Which sentence shows that keeping the same sleep time is difficult for some nurses?
options: "They take short breaks, drink water, and eat light meals."
"…although this is not always possible with family life."
qs.why: although 帶出限制：有家庭生活時不一定做得到。
qs.evidence: although this is not always possible with family life

qs.q: Why do nurses wear sunglasses on the way home?
options: To keep light from waking up the body clock
qs.why: 推論題：文章說光讓身體清醒；下班要回家睡，所以戴墨鏡擋光。這題要把第二段和第三段連起來。
qs.evidence: they wear sunglasses on the way home and sleep in a dark, quiet room

title: The Hidden Sugar in Drinks
paras: Bubble tea, soda, and fruit juice are popular in Taiwan, especially among young people. Many of these drinks contain a surprising amount of sugar. A large cup of sweet milk tea can contain more sugar than a person should have in a whole day.

Sugar in drinks is a special problem because it does not make us feel full. If we eat a piece of cake, we usually eat less at the next meal. But after a sweet drink, most people eat the same amount of food as usual. Over time, these extra calories can lead to weight gain. Too much sugar is also linked to tooth decay and type 2 diabetes.

This does not mean that people can never enjoy a sweet drink. Health educators suggest small changes. Ask for less sugar or no sugar when you order. Choose a smaller cup. Drink water or unsweetened tea with meals, and keep sweet drinks for special occasions.
Nurses often teach these ideas to patients. Simple, practical advice is usually more helpful than telling people to stop completely.
zh: 珍奶、汽水、果汁在台灣很受歡迎，很多含糖量驚人，一大杯甜奶茶的糖可能超過一天該吃的量。飲料的糖特別麻煩，因為喝了不會飽：吃蛋糕下一餐會少吃，喝甜飲料卻照常吃，久了多的熱量會讓人變胖，糖太多也和蛀牙、第二型糖尿病有關。這不代表永遠不能喝，衛教人員建議小改變：點少糖或無糖、選小杯、吃飯配水或無糖茶、甜飲料留到特別場合。護理師常教這些，簡單實用的建議比叫人完全不喝更有效。

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
options: To say that bubble tea should be banned
To compare cake and soda prices
To explain the problem with sugary drinks and give practical advice
qs.why: 先講問題，再給建議，最後說護理師怎麼衛教。

qs.q: Why is sugar in drinks a special problem?
options: It does not make us feel full.
It is more expensive than food.
qs.why: because it does not make us feel full
qs.evidence: it does not make us feel full

qs.q: Which of these is NOT suggested in paragraph 3?
qs.why: 第三段建議少糖、小杯、配水或無糖茶；沒有說每餐喝果汁。注意題目的 NOT。

qs.q: "Tooth decay" is most likely…
qs.why: 跟糖有關的牙齒問題，decay 是「腐壞」，tooth decay 是蛀牙。
qs.evidence: Too much sugar is also linked to tooth decay

qs.q: Which sentence supports the idea that advice should be realistic?
options: "Simple, practical advice is usually more helpful than telling people to stop completely."
"Bubble tea, soda, and fruit juice are popular in Taiwan."
"A large cup of sweet milk tea can contain more sugar than a person should have in a whole day."
qs.why: 最後一句直接說簡單實用的建議比完全禁止更有幫助。
qs.evidence: Simple, practical advice is usually more helpful than telling people to stop completely.

title: When Patients Speak Another Language
paras: Hospitals in many countries care for patients who do not speak the local language well. In the United States, for example, nurses may meet patients who speak Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese, or many other languages.

When a nurse and a patient cannot understand each other, mistakes can happen. A patient may not understand how to take a medicine, or a nurse may miss an important symptom. For this reason, many hospitals provide professional interpreters, either in person or by phone or video.

It might seem easier to ask a family member to translate, but this can cause problems. Family members may not know medical words. They may also change the message because they want to protect the patient from bad news. Children should not be asked to interpret for their parents about serious health matters.
Nurses who speak two languages are very valuable. Still, even bilingual staff need to know when a professional interpreter is the safer choice.
zh: 很多國家的醫院會照顧不太會說當地語言的病人，例如美國的護理師可能遇到說西班牙語、中文、越南語等的病人。互相聽不懂就可能出錯：病人不懂怎麼吃藥，或護理師漏掉重要症狀，所以很多醫院提供專業口譯，現場或電話、視訊。叫家人翻譯看似簡單卻有問題：可能不懂醫學詞、可能為了保護病人改掉壞消息，嚴重的健康問題不應讓小孩幫父母翻譯。雙語護理師很寶貴，但也要知道什麼時候找專業口譯比較安全。

qs.q: Why do many hospitals provide professional interpreters?
options: Because family members are too busy
Because patients ask for them to save money
qs.why: For this reason… 指前一句：聽不懂會出錯。
qs.evidence: For this reason, many hospitals provide professional interpreters

qs.q: Which is a reason the text gives for NOT using family members?
qs.why: They may also change the message because they want to protect the patient from bad news.
qs.evidence: They may also change the message

qs.q: In paragraph 3, "They" in "They may also change the message" refers to…
qs.why: 前一句主詞是 Family members。
qs.evidence: Family members may not know medical words.

qs.q: "Bilingual" (paragraph 4) means…
qs.why: 前一句 Nurses who speak two languages，bilingual 就是雙語的。
qs.evidence: Nurses who speak two languages are very valuable.

qs.q: What is the writer's opinion?
options: Professional interpreters are often the safer choice.
Patients should learn English before going to hospital.
qs.why: 第三段說家人翻譯的問題，最後一段說即使雙語人員也要知道何時找專業口譯更安全。

title: Preventing Falls at Home
paras: Falls are a common reason why older adults go to hospital. A fall can lead to a broken hip, a head injury, or a long time in bed. Even when there is no serious injury, many older people become afraid of falling again, so they move less and become weaker.

Many falls happen at home, and many of them can be prevented. Community nurses often visit older people to look for risks. Common risks include poor lighting, loose rugs, wet bathroom floors, and things left on the stairs. Some medicines, such as sleeping pills, can also make people dizzy.

Small changes can make a big difference. Installing grab bars in the bathroom, using night lights, and wearing shoes with good grip are simple steps. Regular exercise that improves balance and leg strength is also helpful.
Families play an important role too. When they understand the risks, they can help keep the home safe and encourage their parents to stay active.
zh: 跌倒是長者住院的常見原因，可能造成髖骨骨折、頭部受傷或長期臥床；就算沒有重傷，很多人會怕再跌而少動、變得更虛弱。很多跌倒發生在家裡，也多半能預防。社區護理師會家訪找風險：燈光不足、地毯鬆動、浴室地板濕、樓梯上堆東西，有些藥（如安眠藥）也會讓人頭暈。小改變效果很大：浴室裝扶手、用小夜燈、穿止滑的鞋，規律做增強平衡和腿力的運動。家人了解風險後也能幫忙維持居家安全、鼓勵長輩多活動。

qs.q: According to paragraph 1, why do some older people become weaker after a fall?
options: They are afraid of falling again, so they move less.
qs.why: many older people become afraid of falling again, so they move less and become weaker
qs.evidence: so they move less and become weaker

qs.q: Which is NOT mentioned as a fall risk at home?
qs.why: 第二段列出燈光、地毯、濕地板、樓梯雜物、藥物，沒有提到音樂。

qs.q: "Grab bars" are most likely…
options: bars you hold to stop yourself from falling
qs.why: 裝在浴室、用來防跌：grab 是「抓」，grab bars 是扶手。
qs.evidence: Installing grab bars in the bathroom

qs.q: Which sentence tells us that medicine can increase the risk of falling?
options: "Falls are a common reason why older adults go to hospital."
"Some medicines, such as sleeping pills, can also make people dizzy."
qs.why: 頭暈會增加跌倒風險，安眠藥是例子。
qs.evidence: Some medicines, such as sleeping pills, can also make people dizzy.

qs.q: What is the best title?
options: Falls at home: risks and prevention
Why older people should stay in bed
qs.why: 全文說跌倒的影響、居家風險和預防。

title: The Doctor Who Asked Others to Wash Their Hands
paras: In the 1840s, the Vienna General Hospital had two maternity clinics. Women gave birth in both, but many more mothers died of childbed fever in the first clinic than in the second. The difference was so well known that some women begged to be admitted to the second clinic, and a few even preferred to give birth in the street.

Ignaz Semmelweis, a young Hungarian doctor working in the first clinic, wanted to understand why. He noticed that the first clinic was staffed by doctors and medical students, while the second was run by midwives. Importantly, the doctors and students often came directly from performing autopsies on dead bodies.

When a colleague died after being cut by a student's knife during an autopsy, with an illness similar to childbed fever, Semmelweis formed a theory. He believed that 'particles' from the bodies were being carried on the doctors' hands to the women. In 1847, he required staff to wash their hands in a chlorinated lime solution before examining patients. Deaths in the first clinic fell dramatically.

Despite these results, many doctors rejected his ideas. Some were offended by the suggestion that they themselves were causing deaths, and germ theory had not yet been developed to explain the findings. Semmelweis died in 1865, long before his work was widely accepted. Today, he is remembered as an early pioneer of hand hygiene, a practice that remains one of the most effective ways to prevent infections in hospitals.
zh: 1840 年代維也納總醫院有兩個產科病房，第一病房死於產褥熱的產婦遠多於第二病房，有些產婦拜託進第二病房，甚至寧願在街上生。匈牙利年輕醫師塞麥爾維斯在第一病房工作，發現第一病房由醫師和醫學生負責，第二病房由助產士負責，而醫師和學生常剛做完大體解剖就直接過來。一位同事解剖時被學生的刀割傷後死亡，病況類似產褥熱，他推論屍體的「微粒」被醫師的手帶到產婦身上。1847 年他要求工作人員檢查病人前用含氯石灰溶液洗手，第一病房死亡率大幅下降。但很多醫師不接受，有人覺得被冒犯，當時也還沒有細菌理論。他 1865 年過世，遠早於他的研究被普遍接受。今天他被視為手部衛生的先驅。

qs.q: Choose the best heading for paragraph B (the 2nd paragraph).
options: A key difference between the two clinics
qs.why: 第二段在比較兩個病房由誰負責、醫師剛做完解剖，是兩個病房的關鍵差異。

qs.q: Choose the best heading for paragraph D (the 4th paragraph).
options: A key difference between the two clinics
qs.why: 第四段說當時被拒絕，後來才被認可。

qs.q: Statement: More mothers died in the first clinic than in the second clinic.
qs.why: 第一段：many more mothers died … in the first clinic than in the second. 跟敘述一致 → True。
qs.evidence: many more mothers died of childbed fever in the first clinic than in the second

qs.q: Statement: The midwives in the second clinic also performed autopsies.
qs.why: 文章只說醫師和學生常做解剖，沒提助產士有沒有做。沒寫到 → Not Given（不是 False）。
qs.evidence: the doctors and students often came directly from performing autopsies

qs.q: Statement: Most doctors accepted Semmelweis's ideas immediately.
qs.why: 第四段：Semmelweis died in 1865, long before his work was widely accepted —— 他過世時，他的想法都還沒被普遍接受，所以「大多數醫師立刻接受」跟文章相反 → False。（many doctors rejected his ideas 只說「很多人」反對，單靠這句還不能推出「大多數」；真正的證據是「很久以後才被普遍接受」。）
qs.evidence: long before his work was widely accepted

qs.q: What did Semmelweis require in 1847?
options: Washing hands in a chlorinated lime solution before examining patients
qs.why: he required staff to wash their hands in a chlorinated lime solution before examining patients
qs.evidence: he required staff to wash their hands in a chlorinated lime solution before examining patients

qs.q: "Dramatically" in "Deaths … fell dramatically" is closest to…
qs.why: dramatically 表示變化很大、很明顯。

title: Nursing at a Distance
paras: Not long ago, almost all nursing care required the nurse and the patient to be in the same room. Today, telehealth allows some care to be delivered through phone calls, video visits, and devices that send health data from a patient's home to a hospital.

Supporters point out several benefits. Patients who live far from a hospital, or who find it difficult to travel, can receive advice without a long journey. People with long-term conditions, such as heart failure, can have their weight or blood pressure checked every day, so that nurses notice warning signs early. Some studies suggest this kind of monitoring can reduce hospital admissions for certain patients.

However, telehealth also has limits. A nurse cannot touch a swollen leg or smell an infected wound through a screen. Older patients may struggle with technology, and families without a stable internet connection may be left out. There are also concerns about privacy when personal health information is sent online.

Most experts agree that telehealth will not replace face-to-face care but will become part of it. For future nurses, this means new skills: clear communication on camera, careful questioning when physical examination is not possible, and knowing when a patient must be seen in person.
zh: 不久前幾乎所有護理照護都要護理師和病人在同一個房間；現在遠距醫療可以用電話、視訊和把居家健康數據傳到醫院的裝置提供部分照護。支持者指出好處：住得遠或行動不便的人不用長途奔波；心衰竭等慢性病人可以每天測體重或血壓，讓護理師及早發現警訊；有研究顯示這種監測可能減少某些病人住院。但也有限制：隔著螢幕摸不到腫脹的腿、聞不到感染傷口的味道；長者可能不會用科技；網路不穩的家庭可能被排除；健康資料上網也有隱私疑慮。多數專家認為遠距醫療不會取代面對面照護，而是成為其中一部分；未來的護理師需要新技能：鏡頭前清楚溝通、無法身體檢查時仔細問診、知道什麼時候病人一定要親自來。

qs.q: Choose the best heading for paragraph B (the 2nd paragraph).
options: Advantages of care at a distance
qs.why: 第二段列出支持者說的好處。

qs.q: Choose the best heading for paragraph C (the 3rd paragraph).
options: Advantages of care at a distance
qs.why: However 開頭，接著說限制和問題。

qs.q: Statement: Telehealth can help nurses notice warning signs early in some patients.
qs.why: 第二段：so that nurses notice warning signs early → True。
qs.evidence: so that nurses notice warning signs early

qs.q: Statement: Telehealth is cheaper than face-to-face care for all patients.
qs.why: 文章沒有比較費用 → Not Given。小心不要用自己的常識答題。

qs.q: Statement: Experts believe telehealth will completely replace face-to-face care.
qs.why: 最後一段：will not replace face-to-face care → False。
qs.evidence: telehealth will not replace face-to-face care

qs.q: According to paragraph C, why might some families be left out?
options: They do not have a stable internet connection.
They live too close to the hospital.
They do not have long-term conditions.
qs.why: families without a stable internet connection may be left out
qs.evidence: families without a stable internet connection may be left out

qs.q: Which phrase shows a skill future nurses will need?
options: "careful questioning when physical examination is not possible"
qs.why: 最後一段列出新技能，這是其中之一。
qs.evidence: careful questioning when physical examination is not possible

title: Why Nurses Leave
paras: In many countries, hospitals report that it is difficult to keep enough nurses. The problem is not only training new nurses but also keeping experienced ones. When nurses leave the profession early, hospitals lose skills that took years to build.

Surveys of nurses often point to heavy workloads as a main reason for leaving. When one nurse is responsible for too many patients, there is little time for anything beyond essential tasks. Many nurses say this is stressful not only because they are tired, but because they feel they cannot give the quality of care they were trained to provide.

Other factors include irregular shifts, low pay compared with the level of responsibility, and limited opportunities for career development. Experiences of verbal abuse from patients or visitors can also make the job harder.

Some hospitals have tried to respond. Measures include safer staffing levels, mentoring programs for new graduates, flexible scheduling, and support services for staff wellbeing. Researchers note that no single measure is enough on its own; nurses are more likely to stay when several of these improvements work together.
zh: 很多國家的醫院表示很難留住足夠的護理師，問題不只是培養新人，還有留住資深人員；太早離開會讓醫院失去多年累積的技能。調查常指出工作量太大是主要離職原因：一人顧太多病人，只能做最必要的事；很多人說壓力大不只是累，而是覺得無法提供受訓時學到的照護品質。其他因素包括輪班不規律、薪水和責任不成比例、升遷發展機會少，還有被病人或訪客言語暴力。有些醫院開始回應：更安全的人力比、新人導師制、彈性排班、員工身心支持。研究者指出沒有單一措施就夠，多項改善一起做，護理師才更可能留下來。

qs.q: Choose the best heading for paragraph B (the 2nd paragraph).
options: Too much work, too little time
qs.why: 第二段在說工作量太大、時間不夠。

qs.q: Choose the best heading for paragraph D (the 4th paragraph).
options: Too much work, too little time
qs.why: Some hospitals have tried to respond… 接著列措施。

qs.q: Statement: According to surveys, heavy workload is a main reason nurses leave.
qs.why: 第二段第一句 → True。
qs.evidence: Surveys of nurses often point to heavy workloads as a main reason for leaving.

qs.q: Statement: Nurses feel stressed only because they are physically tired.
qs.why: 文章說 not only because they are tired, but because…，所以「只因為累」是錯的 → False。
qs.evidence: not only because they are tired

qs.q: Statement: Mentoring programs are more effective than flexible scheduling.
qs.why: 文章列了兩者，但沒有比較哪個比較有效 → Not Given。

qs.q: What do researchers say about the measures?
options: Several improvements working together help most.
qs.why: no single measure is enough on its own; nurses are more likely to stay when several of these improvements work together
qs.evidence: nurses are more likely to stay when several of these improvements work together

qs.q: "Verbal abuse" (paragraph C) means…
qs.why: verbal 是「言語的」，abuse 是「傷害、虐待」，合起來是言語暴力。

title: The Night the Lights Went Out
paras: It was just after two in the morning, and most of the patients on Ward 7 were sleeping. I was checking the drip of an elderly man in Bed 12 while my colleague, Ming, was writing up her notes at the nurses' station. Outside, a storm had been building for hours, but none of us had paid much attention to it.

Then, without any warning, the lights went out. For a few seconds the ward was completely dark and silent, apart from the rain hitting the windows. A patient called out in fear. I remember thinking that I had never heard the ward so quiet before. Then the emergency lights came on, and the machines beside the beds began to beep as they switched to battery power.

Ming and I knew what to do, because the hospital had run a power-cut drill only two weeks earlier. She went to check the patients who were on oxygen, while I walked from bed to bed with a torch, telling people that they were safe and that the power would soon return. Mr. Wu in Bed 3, who had arrived that afternoon after a fall, was trying to climb out of bed. He was confused and thought he was at home. I sat with him and held his hand until he calmed down.

The main power came back after about twenty minutes, but it felt much longer. When the day staff arrived at seven, we told them everything that had happened. The head nurse said that the drill had clearly been worth the time it took.

I used to think that drills were a waste of time. I used to stand at the back and check my phone while the trainer was talking. That night changed my mind. Now, whenever we practise for an emergency, I pay attention, because I know that one day it might be real.
zh: 凌晨兩點多，病房大多數病人在睡。作者正在幫 12 床的老先生檢查點滴，同事 Ming 在護理站寫紀錄；外面的暴風雨已經醞釀好幾個小時，但沒人注意。突然停電，病房一片黑，有病人害怕地叫出聲；接著緊急照明亮起，床邊的機器切換到電池而嗶嗶叫。因為兩週前醫院才做過停電演練，她們知道怎麼做：Ming 去看用氧氣的病人，作者拿手電筒逐床安撫。當天下午跌倒住院的 3 床吳先生搞不清楚狀況想爬下床，作者握著他的手直到他平靜。大約二十分鐘後復電。作者以前覺得演練浪費時間，那一晚之後改觀，現在每次演練都認真聽。

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a nurse and her colleague handled a power cut at night
Why storms often cause power cuts in hospitals
How to train new nurses for night shifts
qs.why: 整篇在講停電那一晚她們怎麼處理，最後說作者對演練的看法改變了。

qs.q: What was the writer doing when the lights went out?
options: Writing notes at the nurses' station
qs.why: 第一段：I was checking the drip…——過去進行式 was checking 是停電那一刻正在做的事；在寫紀錄的是 Ming。
qs.evidence: I was checking the drip of an elderly man in Bed 12

qs.q: Statement: The hospital had practised for a power cut before that night.
qs.why: had run 是過去完成式：在停電「之前」就做過演練（two weeks earlier）→ True。
qs.evidence: the hospital had run a power-cut drill only two weeks earlier

qs.q: In "until he calmed down", who does "he" refer to?
qs.why: 前面兩句都在講 3 床的吳先生（Mr. Wu），he 指他。
qs.evidence: I sat with him and held his hand until he calmed down.

qs.q: Statement: The writer has always taken emergency drills seriously.
qs.why: used to 表示「以前這樣、現在不是了」：她以前覺得演練浪費時間，那晚之後才改觀 → False。
qs.evidence: I used to think that drills were a waste of time.

title: Mary Seacole: The Nurse Who Went Anyway
paras: Mary Seacole was born in Kingston, Jamaica, in 1805. Her mother ran a boarding house and was known as a 'doctress', a woman who treated sick people with traditional medicine. As a girl, Mary used to watch her mother at work, and by the time she was a young woman, she had learned a great deal about caring for the sick.

As an adult, Seacole travelled widely. In the early 1850s she was living in Panama when cholera broke out there. She had seen the disease before in Jamaica, so she knew how to nurse people through it, and she treated many patients.

In 1854, news reached Britain that British soldiers were dying in the Crimean War, many of them from disease rather than from their wounds. Seacole travelled to London and offered to go to the war as a nurse. However, her application was turned down. She later wrote that she wondered whether this had happened because of the colour of her skin.

Seacole did not give up. She decided to pay for the journey herself. With a business partner, she set up the 'British Hotel' near the battlefront, a place where officers could buy food and supplies and where sick and wounded soldiers could get care. She often rode out to the battlefield itself, carrying medicine and food.

When the war ended, Seacole returned to London with very little money, as her business had failed. In 1857 she published a book about her life, which became popular. For many years after her death in 1881 she was largely forgotten, but in 2016 a statue of her was put up in the grounds of St Thomas' Hospital in London.
zh: 瑪麗．西戈爾 1805 年生於牙買加京斯敦，母親經營寄宿旅館，也用傳統醫術照顧病人；她從小看母親工作，長大時已經學會很多照顧病人的知識。成年後她到處旅行，1850 年代初住在巴拿馬時遇上霍亂，因為之前在牙買加就見過這種病，所以知道怎麼照護。1854 年英國士兵在克里米亞戰爭中大量死亡，很多是死於疾病。她到倫敦申請當隨軍護士卻被拒絕，她後來寫道懷疑是因為膚色。她沒有放棄，自費前往，和合夥人在前線附近開了「英國旅館」，賣食物補給，也照顧傷病士兵，還常騎馬到戰場送藥和食物。戰後她生意失敗、幾乎沒錢；1857 年出版自傳並暢銷。她 1881 年過世後長期被遺忘，2016 年倫敦聖湯瑪士醫院立了她的雕像。

qs.q: How did Mary Seacole first learn about caring for the sick?
options: By training at a hospital in London
By working as a soldier's assistant
qs.why: 第一段：As a girl, Mary used to watch her mother at work——used to 是小時候常做的事。
qs.evidence: As a girl, Mary used to watch her mother at work

qs.q: Why did Seacole know how to treat cholera patients in Panama?
options: She had studied it at university.
She had seen the disease before in Jamaica.
A doctor in Panama had taught her.
qs.why: had seen 是過去完成式：到巴拿馬「之前」就在牙買加見過霍亂。
qs.evidence: She had seen the disease before in Jamaica

qs.q: Statement: The British government paid for Seacole's journey to the war.
qs.why: 文章說她被拒絕之後決定自己出錢（pay for the journey herself）→ False。
qs.evidence: She decided to pay for the journey herself.

qs.q: Statement: The British Hotel was the largest building near the battlefront.
qs.why: 文章只說旅館在前線附近、賣什麼、照顧誰，完全沒提大小 → Not Given。

qs.q: In paragraph 3, 'turned down' is closest in meaning to…
qs.why: her application was turned down：申請被「拒絕」，後面她才決定自己去。
qs.evidence: However, her application was turned down.

title: The Wrong Bus
paras: On the first morning of my clinical placement, I woke up an hour early. I had laid out my uniform the night before, and I had checked the bus route three times. I was determined not to be late.

At the bus stop, I was reading my notes on infection control when a bus pulled up. I glanced at the number, saw a seven, and climbed on. Only after ten minutes did I realise that I had taken the number 17, not the number 7. By then, we were heading in completely the wrong direction.

I got off at the next stop and stood on the pavement, feeling sick. My phone battery was almost dead, because I had been studying on it all morning. I used to panic in situations like this, but my placement teacher had told us something useful: 'When things go wrong, call early.' So I called the ward and explained what had happened.

The nurse who answered was calm. She told me which bus to take and said that the morning handover would not start until half past seven. When I finally walked onto the ward, twenty minutes late and out of breath, she was waiting for me. 'You called before we started worrying,' she said. 'That's exactly what we want from a nurse.'
I still feel embarrassed when I think about that morning. But I learned two things: check the number twice, and when you make a mistake, tell someone straight away.
zh: 實習第一天作者提早一小時起床，前一晚就把制服準備好、公車路線查了三次。在公車站讀感染控制筆記時，她瞄到號碼有個 7 就上車，十分鐘後才發現搭的是 17 號，方向完全相反。她下車時手機快沒電（整個早上都在用手機讀書）。她以前遇到這種事會慌，但實習老師說過「出狀況就早點打電話」，於是她打給病房說明。接電話的護理師很冷靜，告訴她搭哪班車，說交班七點半才開始。她遲到二十分鐘、氣喘吁吁地到病房，那位護理師說：「你在我們開始擔心之前就打來了，這正是我們希望護理師做的。」她學到兩件事：號碼看兩次；犯錯就馬上告訴別人。

qs.q: What is the main lesson the writer learned?
options: Taking the bus is not a good way to get to work.
It is better to report a problem early than to hide it.
Students should not study on their phones.
qs.why: 最後一段：when you make a mistake, tell someone straight away；護理師也稱讚她早點打電話。

qs.q: Why did the writer get on the wrong bus?
options: She did not look at the number carefully.
The bus driver gave her wrong information.
Her usual bus had been cancelled.
qs.why: 她只是 glanced（瞄一眼），看到 7 就上車，其實是 17。
qs.evidence: I glanced at the number, saw a seven, and climbed on.

qs.q: Which sentence best shows that the writer had prepared carefully?
options: I had laid out my uniform the night before, and I had checked the bus route three times.
I got off at the next stop and stood on the pavement, feeling sick.
I still feel embarrassed when I think about that morning.
qs.why: 過去完成式 had laid out、had checked：出門「之前」就準備好了。
qs.evidence: I had laid out my uniform the night before, and I had checked the bus route three times.

qs.q: Statement: The writer's phone was almost out of battery because she had used it to study.
qs.why: because I had been studying on it all morning：電快沒了的原因就是整個早上用它讀書 → True。
qs.evidence: My phone battery was almost dead, because I had been studying on it all morning.

qs.q: Statement: The nurse on the ward was angry that the writer was late.
qs.why: 接電話的護理師很冷靜（calm），還稱讚她早點打電話 → False。
qs.evidence: The nurse who answered was calm.

title: Your Clinical Placement: What to Expect
topic: 橋接 44：未來安排、未來進行式和未來完成式
paras: Dear second-year students, your first clinical placement starts on Monday, 3 March, and lasts four weeks. This email explains what you will be doing and what you will need to bring. Please read it carefully before your orientation meeting next Friday.

During the first week, you won't be working with patients on your own. Instead, each of you will be following an experienced nurse, called your mentor, for the whole shift. You will be watching how your mentor plans the day, talks to patients and records information. Your mentor will be expecting you to ask questions, so please do not be shy.

From the second week, you will be taking care of one or two patients yourselves, with your mentor checking your work. By the end of the second week, you will have practised taking vital signs, giving oral medication under supervision and writing simple nursing notes. In week three, you will be presenting a short case study to your group.

The morning shift starts with handover at 7:30 a.m., so please arrive by 7:15. Please bring your student ID card, a watch with a second hand, and a small notebook. Phones must be kept in your locker during the shift.

By the time the placement finishes, you will have completed about 120 hours on the ward. On the last day, you and your mentor will be meeting to discuss your progress. If you have any questions before then, I will be holding an online question session this Wednesday at 6 p.m. Best wishes, Ms. Lin, Clinical Coordinator
zh: 臨床實習協調員林老師寫給二年級學生的信：第一次實習 3 月 3 日（週一）開始，為期四週。第一週不會自己照顧病人，而是整個班跟著一位資深護理師（導師），看她怎麼安排一天、跟病人溝通、做紀錄，導師會期待學生發問。第二週起自己照顧一到兩位病人，導師會檢查；第二週結束前會練習量生命徵象、在督導下給口服藥、寫簡單的護理紀錄；第三週要向小組報告個案。早班七點半交班，請七點十五分前到，帶學生證、有秒針的手錶和小筆記本，手機要放置物櫃。實習結束時會累積約 120 小時，最後一天和導師面談進度；週三晚上六點有線上問答。

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this email?
options: To tell students what will happen during their placement
To invite students to apply for a job
To explain how to become a mentor
qs.why: 開頭就說這封信說明 what you will be doing and what you will need to bring。

qs.q: What will students be doing in the first week?
qs.why: will be following 是未來進行式：第一週那段時間「正在」跟著導師。照顧病人是第二週，報告是第三週。
qs.evidence: each of you will be following an experienced nurse, called your mentor, for the whole shift

qs.q: Statement: By the end of week two, students will have practised giving oral medication under supervision.
qs.why: By the end of the second week, you will have practised…——未來完成式：在第二週結束「之前」就會練過 → True。
qs.evidence: By the end of the second week, you will have practised taking vital signs, giving oral medication under supervision

qs.q: Statement: Students may keep their phones with them during the shift if the phones are on silent.
qs.why: 信上說手機一定要放在置物櫃（must be kept in your locker），沒有「靜音就可以」→ False。
qs.evidence: Phones must be kept in your locker during the shift.

qs.q: Statement: The online question session will be recorded for students who cannot attend.
qs.why: 只說週三晚上六點有線上問答，沒提會不會錄影 → Not Given。

title: The Year Ahead: Planning Your Final Year
topic: 橋接 44：未來安排、未來進行式和未來完成式
paras: For many nursing students, the final year feels like a race. You will be finishing your last clinical placements, writing reports and, at the same time, preparing for the licensing exam. Without a plan, it is easy to feel that you are always running behind.

Experienced teachers suggest starting with the end in mind. Write down the date of your exam, and then work backwards. Ask yourself: what will I need to have finished by then? For example, if your exam is in July, you might decide that by the end of March you will have reviewed every subject once, and by the end of May you will have done at least three full practice tests.

Next, look at the weeks when you will be busy with other things. If you know that you will be working night shifts on a placement in April, do not plan heavy study for that month. Instead, plan short review sessions, such as fifteen minutes of flashcards on the bus.

It also helps to tell other people about your plan. If your family knows that you will be studying every Saturday morning, they are less likely to ask you to do other things at that time. Some students form study groups and agree on goals: 'By next Friday, we'll have finished the cardiovascular chapter.'

Finally, remember to plan rest. A student who is studying fourteen hours a day in June will probably be exhausted by July. This time next year, you will be wearing your own uniform and working as a qualified nurse. The aim is to arrive there healthy, not burnt out.
zh: 對很多護理系學生來說，最後一年像在賽跑：要完成最後的實習、寫報告，同時準備國考，沒有計畫就會一直覺得落後。老師建議從終點往回推：寫下考試日期，問自己到那時要完成什麼——例如七月考，就訂三月底前每科都複習過一次、五月底前至少做完三回完整模擬考。接著看哪幾週會忙別的事，例如四月實習要上大夜，就別排重的讀書計畫，改成短時間複習，像在公車上看十五分鐘字卡。把計畫告訴別人也有幫助：家人知道你每週六早上要讀書，就比較不會那時找你做別的事；有些人組讀書會一起訂目標。最後要記得安排休息：六月每天讀十四小時的人，到七月大概已經累垮。明年這時候你會穿著自己的制服當正式護理師，目標是健康地抵達，而不是燃燒殆盡。

qs.q: What is the writer's main advice?
options: Study as many hours as possible every day.
Make a plan that works backwards from the exam date.
Avoid clinical placements in the final year.
qs.why: 第二段的核心：Write down the date of your exam, and then work backwards，後面幾段都是怎麼排這個計畫。

qs.q: According to paragraph 3, what should students do in a month with night shifts?
options: Plan short review sessions instead of heavy study
qs.why: 第三段：do not plan heavy study… Instead, plan short review sessions。
qs.evidence: Instead, plan short review sessions

qs.q: In "they are less likely to ask you to do other things", what does "they" refer to?
qs.why: 同一句前半句的主詞是 your family，they 指家人。
qs.evidence: If your family knows that you will be studying every Saturday morning, they are less likely to ask you to do other things at that time.

qs.q: In paragraph 5, 'burnt out' is closest in meaning to…
options: extremely tired from too much work
qs.why: 前一句說每天讀十四小時會 exhausted（累垮），burnt out 就是長期太累、耗盡。
qs.evidence: The aim is to arrive there healthy, not burnt out.

qs.q: Statement: The writer says study groups always produce better exam results.
qs.why: 文章只說有些人組讀書會一起訂目標，沒說讀書會的成績一定比較好 → Not Given。

title: Orientation Week for New Staff
topic: 橋接 44：未來安排、未來進行式和未來完成式
paras: Welcome to Riverside General Hospital. We are delighted that you are joining our nursing team. Your orientation week begins on Monday, 1 September. During this week you will not be assigned any patients. Instead, you will be getting to know the hospital, its systems and the people you will be working with.

On Monday morning, you will be attending a welcome talk by the Director of Nursing, followed by a tour of the main building. In the afternoon, the IT team will be setting up your account for the electronic health record system, so please bring your staff card.

Tuesday and Wednesday are training days. You will be practising emergency procedures, including basic life support, in our simulation centre. By Wednesday afternoon, you will have completed the fire safety course, which every member of staff must pass before working on a ward.

On Thursday, you will be spending the whole day on the ward where you will work, shadowing a senior nurse. This is a good chance to learn the ward routine and to ask questions. On Friday, you will be meeting your preceptor, an experienced nurse who will support you during your first three months.

By the end of the week, you will have met most of the people you need to know, and you will have a clear idea of what your first month will look like. Lunch will be provided every day in the staff canteen. If you are unable to attend any part of the programme, please let the education office know as soon as possible.
zh: 歡迎新進護理人員的信：新人訓練週 9 月 1 日（週一）開始，這週不會分配病人，而是認識醫院、系統和同事。週一上午聽護理部主任致詞、參觀主大樓，下午資訊組會幫你開電子病歷帳號，所以要帶員工證。週二、週三是訓練日，在模擬中心練習急救流程（含基本救命術）；週三下午前要完成消防安全課程，所有員工都要通過才能上病房。週四整天到自己未來的病房跟著資深護理師見習；週五和你的臨床輔導員（preceptor）見面，她會在前三個月支持你。週末時你會認識大部分需要認識的人，也會清楚第一個月的樣子。每天在員工餐廳供應午餐；不能參加的部分要盡快告訴教育室。

qs.q: What is this text mainly about?
options: The plan for new nurses' first week
How to apply for a job at the hospital
The history of Riverside General Hospital
qs.why: 整封信一天一天說明新人訓練週要做什麼。

qs.q: Why should new staff bring their staff card on Monday?
options: So that their computer account can be set up
qs.why: 週一下午資訊組要幫你開電子病歷帳號，so please bring your staff card。
qs.evidence: the IT team will be setting up your account for the electronic health record system, so please bring your staff card

qs.q: Statement: New staff must pass the fire safety course before they work on a ward.
qs.why: 消防課程 every member of staff must pass before working on a ward → True。
qs.evidence: which every member of staff must pass before working on a ward

qs.q: Statement: New nurses will look after two patients on Thursday.
qs.why: 第一段就說這一週不會分配任何病人（not be assigned any patients），週四是見習 → False。
qs.evidence: During this week you will not be assigned any patients.

qs.q: In paragraph 4, a 'preceptor' is…
options: a nurse who supports a new nurse during the first months
a computer system for patient records
a patient who has just been admitted
qs.why: 逗號後面就是解釋：an experienced nurse who will support you during your first three months。
qs.evidence: your preceptor, an experienced nurse who will support you during your first three months

title: Reading the Clues: Sudden Confusion in Older Patients
paras: Mrs. Huang, an 82-year-old woman, had been on the orthopaedic ward for three days after a hip operation. She had been chatting happily with the nurses every morning. But on the fourth morning, she did not recognise her own daughter and kept asking where she was. Her daughter was shocked. 'She must be getting dementia,' she said.

The nurse, however, was not so sure. Dementia usually develops slowly, over months or years. Mrs. Huang had changed overnight. A sudden change like this is called delirium, and in older patients it can have many causes, including infection, dehydration, pain and certain medicines.

The nurse began to look for clues. Mrs. Huang's water jug was still full from the night before, so she might not have been drinking enough. Her temperature was slightly raised, and her urine was dark and smelled strong. 'She could have a urinary tract infection,' the nurse thought. She also checked the medication chart. A new sleeping pill had been started two nights earlier. That might have played a part too.

The nurse did not try to make a diagnosis herself. Instead, she reported her observations to the doctor clearly: what had changed, when it had changed and what she had noticed. Tests later showed that Mrs. Huang did have an infection. With antibiotics, fluids and a change in her medicines, she was back to her usual self within a few days.

This case shows why nurses should never assume that confusion in an older person is 'just old age'. A family member may conclude that nothing can be done, but a careful nurse asks a different question: what must have changed, and why?
zh: 82 歲的黃太太髖關節手術後在骨科病房住了三天，每天早上都跟護理師聊得很開心；第四天早上卻認不出自己的女兒、一直問自己在哪裡。女兒嚇到，說她一定是失智了。護理師不這麼確定：失智通常是幾個月、幾年慢慢發生，黃太太卻是一夜之間改變。這種突然的改變叫譫妄，老人家的原因很多，包括感染、脫水、疼痛和某些藥物。護理師開始找線索：水壺從前一晚到現在還是滿的，可能喝得不夠；體溫稍高、尿色深而且味道重，可能是泌尿道感染；兩天前開始吃一種新的安眠藥，也可能有影響。她沒有自己下診斷，而是清楚地向醫師報告觀察：什麼改變了、什麼時候改變、注意到什麼。檢查證實是感染，用了抗生素、補充水分、調整藥物後，幾天內就恢復了。這個案例說明不能把老人的混亂當成「只是老了」，細心的護理師會問：一定是哪裡改變了？為什麼？

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Older patients often get dementia after operations.
Sudden confusion can have a cause that needs to be looked for.
Families should not visit patients after surgery.
qs.why: 整篇是護理師不接受「一定是失智」，找線索、報告，最後找到原因；最後一段說要問 what must have changed, and why。

qs.q: Why did the nurse doubt that Mrs. Huang had dementia?
options: Because dementia usually develops slowly, but Mrs. Huang changed overnight
Because Mrs. Huang's daughter was a doctor
Because Mrs. Huang was too young for dementia
qs.why: 第二段：失智通常慢慢發生（over months or years），黃太太卻是一夜之間改變。
qs.evidence: Mrs. Huang had changed overnight.

qs.q: Which clue suggested that Mrs. Huang might not have been drinking enough?
options: Her water jug was still full from the night before.
A new sleeping pill had been started.
She did not recognise her daughter.
qs.why: 水壺從前一晚到現在還是滿的 → so she might not have been drinking enough（might have + 過去分詞：推測過去）。
qs.evidence: Mrs. Huang's water jug was still full from the night before

qs.q: Statement: The nurse told the doctor that Mrs. Huang had a urinary tract infection.
qs.why: 護理師心裡想「可能」是泌尿道感染（could have），但她沒有自己下診斷，只報告觀察 → False。
qs.evidence: The nurse did not try to make a diagnosis herself.

qs.q: Statement: Mrs. Huang's daughter visited her every day.
qs.why: 文章只說第四天早上女兒在場，沒說她是不是每天來 → Not Given。

title: What Old Bones Can Tell Us
paras: When archaeologists find a human skeleton, they cannot ask the person any questions. Instead, they have to work like detectives, using small clues to build a picture of a life that ended long ago.

Bones can reveal a surprising amount. The shape of the pelvis, for example, usually shows whether the person was male or female. The teeth give clues about age: a skeleton with all its adult teeth, but with little wear on them, probably belonged to a young adult. Heavy wear suggests that the person must have eaten rough, hard food for many years.

Some of the most interesting clues are injuries. A break that shows no sign of healing tells archaeologists that the person must have died at or around the time of the injury. A break that has healed, on the other hand, means the person lived for weeks or even years afterwards.

Healed injuries can also tell us something about how people treated each other. Imagine a skeleton with a badly broken thigh bone that healed. A person with such an injury could not have walked, hunted or gathered food for many weeks. They can't have survived alone. Someone must have brought them food and water, kept them warm and protected them. In other words, someone must have cared for them.

Of course, archaeologists have to be careful. Bones alone may not tell the whole story, and different experts sometimes reach different conclusions from the same evidence. But when the clues point in the same direction, they allow us to imagine the lives, and sometimes the kindness, of people who lived thousands of years ago.
zh: 考古學家找到人骨時沒辦法問問題，只能像偵探一樣用小線索拼出很久以前的生活。骨頭透露的資訊多得驚人：骨盆形狀通常看得出男女；牙齒是年齡線索——成人牙齒都在但磨損少，大概是年輕人；磨損很重表示這個人一定長年吃粗硬的食物。受傷也是重要線索：骨折完全沒有癒合，代表這人一定是在受傷當時或前後死亡；骨折癒合了，代表他之後又活了幾週甚至幾年。癒合的傷也透露人與人之間怎麼相待：大腿骨嚴重骨折又癒合的人，好幾週不可能走路、打獵或採集食物，不可能獨自活下來，一定有人送食物和水、幫他保暖、保護他——也就是有人照顧過他。當然考古學家必須小心：光靠骨頭不一定看得到全貌，不同專家對同樣的證據有時會有不同結論；但線索都指向同一方向時，我們就能想像幾千年前的人怎麼生活，有時還能看見他們的善良。

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How archaeologists use clues from bones to learn about past lives
Why ancient people often broke their legs
How to look after a broken thigh bone
qs.why: 第一段就說考古學家像偵探用小線索拼出過去的生活，後面一段段舉骨盆、牙齒、骨折的例子。

qs.q: What does heavy wear on the teeth suggest?
options: The person ate rough, hard food for many years.
The person died from an injury.
qs.why: must have eaten：根據磨損「很確定」推測過去吃了很多年粗硬的食物。
qs.evidence: Heavy wear suggests that the person must have eaten rough, hard food for many years.

qs.q: What does a break with no sign of healing tell archaeologists?
options: The person lived for years after the injury.
The person died at or around the time of the injury.
The person was cared for by others.
qs.why: 沒有癒合 → must have died at or around the time of the injury；癒合的才代表之後還活著。
qs.evidence: the person must have died at or around the time of the injury

qs.q: In paragraph 4, in "They can't have survived alone", who does "They" refer to?
options: The person with the broken thigh bone
The people who brought food and water
qs.why: 前一句的主詞是 A person with such an injury；they 用來指這個（性別不明的）人。can't have survived = 推測過去「不可能」活下來。
qs.evidence: They can't have survived alone.

qs.q: Statement: Experts always agree about what bones show.
qs.why: 最後一段：不同專家有時會從同樣的證據得出不同結論 → False。
qs.evidence: different experts sometimes reach different conclusions from the same evidence

title: The Mystery of the Thank-You Card
paras: One Monday morning, a small blue envelope appeared on the desk at the nurses' station on Ward 9. Inside was a card with a drawing of a cat and four words: 'Thank you for everything.' There was no name, and nobody had seen who had left it.

The nurses started guessing. 'It must be from Mr. Lo,' said Grace. 'He went home on Saturday, and he was always talking about his cat.' But Peter shook his head. 'It can't be from Mr. Lo. He broke his right wrist, and this writing is very neat. He couldn't have written it himself.'

'Maybe his wife wrote it for him,' Grace suggested. Peter thought for a moment. 'She might have. But look at the envelope. It's completely dry, and it rained heavily all weekend. Whoever left it must have come in this morning, after the rain stopped.'

Then Lily, a student nurse, noticed something else. The cat had been drawn with a purple crayon, the kind of crayon that young children use. 'It might have been a child,' she said. 'Didn't Mr. Lo's granddaughter visit him every afternoon? She was always drawing.'

At lunchtime, the mystery was solved. Mr. Lo's granddaughter came back to pick up a scarf that he had left behind. When she saw the card on the desk, she smiled shyly. 'Grandpa told me what to write,' she said. 'I did the cat by myself.'
zh: 某個週一早上，9 病房護理站桌上出現一個藍色小信封，裡面的卡片畫了一隻貓，寫著「謝謝你們所做的一切」，沒有署名，也沒人看到是誰放的。護理師們開始猜：Grace 說一定是週六出院的羅先生，他老是聊他的貓；Peter 搖頭說不可能，羅先生右手腕骨折，這字又很工整，他不可能自己寫。Grace 說也許是太太代寫，Peter 說有可能，但信封完全是乾的，整個週末都在下大雨，放卡片的人一定是今天早上雨停後才來的。學生護理師 Lily 又注意到：貓是用紫色蠟筆畫的，那是小孩用的蠟筆，可能是小孩畫的——羅先生的孫女不是每天下午都來、一直在畫畫嗎？中午謎底揭曉：羅先生的孫女回來拿他忘了帶走的圍巾，看到卡片害羞地笑著說：「爺爺告訴我要寫什麼，貓是我自己畫的。」

qs.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: Nurses using clues to work out who left a card
A patient who lost his cat
qs.why: 整篇是護理師們一個線索一個線索推測卡片是誰留的，最後解開謎底。

qs.q: Why did Peter think Mr. Lo couldn't have written the card himself?
options: Mr. Lo had broken his right wrist.
Mr. Lo could not write English.
Mr. Lo had left the hospital a week earlier.
qs.why: Peter 說羅先生右手腕骨折、字又很工整 → He couldn't have written it himself。
qs.evidence: He broke his right wrist, and this writing is very neat.

qs.q: Which clue showed that the card had been left that morning?
options: The card had a drawing of a cat.
qs.why: 整個週末下大雨，信封卻是乾的 → must have come in this morning, after the rain stopped。
qs.evidence: It's completely dry, and it rained heavily all weekend.

qs.q: In "Whoever left it must have come in this morning", 'whoever' means…
options: the person who did it, although we do not know who
everyone who came to the ward
qs.why: whoever = 不管是誰、那個（不知道是誰的）人。
qs.evidence: Whoever left it must have come in this morning

qs.q: Statement: Mr. Lo's granddaughter wrote the words without any help.
qs.why: 她說 Grandpa told me what to write：字是爺爺告訴她要寫什麼，只有貓是自己畫的 → False。
qs.evidence: 'Grandpa told me what to write,' she said.

title: A Near Miss on Ward 5
paras: Late one evening on a busy medical ward, a nurse named Annie prepared a dose of insulin for a patient called Mr. Chen Wei. A few minutes later, she walked into Room 12, where a patient called Mr. Chen Wen-li was sleeping. The names were similar, the two men were about the same age, and both of them had diabetes.

Annie was about to give the injection when she stopped and checked the patient's wristband. The name on the band was not the one on her chart. She went back to the nurses' station, found the right patient and gave him his insulin. Nobody was harmed.

If Annie hadn't checked the wristband, Mr. Chen Wen-li would have received a dose of insulin that he did not need, and his blood sugar could have dropped dangerously low. Looking back, Annie said that she had been rushing because three call bells were ringing at the same time. 'If I had been less busy, I wouldn't have walked into the wrong room in the first place,' she admitted.

Annie reported the near miss, even though no harm had been done. The ward manager thanked her. Because of her report, the ward made two changes. Patients with similar names are now placed in rooms far apart, and a bright 'name alert' sticker is put on their charts and wristbands. Staff must also check two identifiers, such as the patient's full name and date of birth, before giving any medicine.

Some nurses worry that reporting a mistake will get them into trouble. But if Annie had kept quiet, the same thing might have happened to another nurse, and next time the patient might not have been so lucky. A near miss, the ward manager says, is a free lesson.
zh: 某天晚上在忙碌的內科病房，護理師 Annie 幫病人陳偉準備了一劑胰島素，幾分鐘後走進 12 號房，裡面睡的是陳文立——名字很像、年紀差不多、兩人都有糖尿病。她正要打針時停下來核對手圈，發現名字和她的單子不一樣，於是回護理站找到正確的病人。沒有人受傷。如果她沒核對手圈，陳文立就會打到不需要的胰島素，血糖可能危險地降低。她回想當時三個呼叫鈴同時在響，自己太趕；她承認，如果沒那麼忙，一開始就不會走錯房間。雖然沒造成傷害，她還是通報了這次「跡近錯失」，護理長謝謝她。病房因此做了兩項改變：名字相近的病人房間分開，病歷和手圈貼上醒目的「姓名警示」貼紙；給藥前一定要核對兩種身分資料，例如全名和生日。有些護理師擔心通報會惹麻煩，但如果 Annie 沒說，同樣的事可能發生在別人身上，下一位病人可能就沒那麼幸運。護理長說，跡近錯失是一堂免費的課。

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To show how one reported near miss led to safer practice
To describe a nurse who lost her job
qs.why: 從差點出錯、通報、到病房改流程，最後說 a near miss is a free lesson。

qs.q: Why did Annie walk into the wrong room?
options: She had been rushing because several call bells were ringing.
The room numbers had been changed.
The patient had moved to another bed.
qs.why: 第三段：she had been rushing because three call bells were ringing at the same time。
qs.evidence: she had been rushing because three call bells were ringing at the same time

qs.q: What could have happened if Annie had not checked the wristband?
options: The patient's blood sugar could have dropped dangerously low.
The patient would have missed his medicine.
The patient would have been moved to another ward.
qs.why: If Annie hadn't checked…, … could have dropped dangerously low：第三類假設，說「當時沒發生」的後果。
qs.evidence: his blood sugar could have dropped dangerously low

qs.q: Statement: Patients with similar names are now placed in rooms close to each other.
qs.why: 改成 far apart（分開很遠），不是靠近 → False。
qs.evidence: Patients with similar names are now placed in rooms far apart

qs.q: Statement: Annie was given an award for reporting the near miss.
qs.why: 文章只說護理長謝謝她（thanked her），沒提到獎項 → Not Given。

title: The Dirty Dish That Changed Medicine
paras: In the summer of 1928, the Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming went on holiday. Before he left his laboratory at St Mary's Hospital in London, he piled up a number of glass dishes in which he had been growing bacteria. He was not known for keeping a tidy lab.

When he came back in September, he started sorting through the dishes. On one of them, he noticed something strange. A mould had grown on the dish, and around it the bacteria had disappeared. Something produced by the mould seemed to be killing them. Fleming called this substance 'penicillin'.

Historians often point out how much luck was involved. If Fleming had cleaned his dishes before his holiday, he would never have seen the mould. If the weather had been different that summer, the mould and the bacteria might not have grown in the way they did. And if Fleming hadn't looked at the dish carefully before throwing it away, the discovery might have been lost.

However, luck was not enough. Fleming found it very difficult to produce penicillin in large amounts, and for about ten years little progress was made. Then, around 1940, a team at the University of Oxford led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain found a way to purify it and showed that it could cure infections, first in animals and then in people. During the Second World War, factories began to make it on a large scale, and it saved many soldiers who would otherwise have died from infected wounds.

In 1945, Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the Nobel Prize. Fleming himself often said that he had found something he was not looking for. But, as the story shows, an accident only matters if someone notices it and understands what it means.
zh: 1928 年夏天，蘇格蘭科學家弗萊明去度假，離開倫敦聖瑪麗醫院的實驗室前，把一堆培養細菌的玻璃皿疊在一起——他的實驗室向來不太整齊。九月回來整理時，他發現其中一個培養皿長了黴菌，黴菌周圍的細菌都不見了，好像黴菌產生的某種物質把細菌殺死了；他把這種物質叫做盤尼西林。歷史學家常指出這裡面有很多運氣：如果他度假前把培養皿洗乾淨，就永遠不會看到黴菌；如果那年夏天天氣不同，黴菌和細菌可能不會那樣生長；如果他丟掉前沒仔細看，這個發現可能就沒了。但光有運氣不夠：弗萊明很難大量生產盤尼西林，大約十年沒什麼進展；1940 年左右，牛津大學由弗洛里和柴恩帶領的團隊找到純化的方法，證明它能治療感染，先在動物、後在人身上。二戰期間工廠大量生產，救了很多原本會死於傷口感染的士兵。1945 年三人共同獲得諾貝爾獎。弗萊明常說自己找到的是沒在找的東西；但這個故事說明，意外只有在有人注意到、而且懂得它的意義時才重要。

qs.q: What did Fleming notice on one of the dishes?
options: The bacteria around a mould had disappeared.
The bacteria had grown much faster.
qs.why: 第二段：around it the bacteria had disappeared——黴菌周圍的細菌不見了。
qs.evidence: around it the bacteria had disappeared

qs.q: Which sentence shows that Fleming's lab was not very tidy?
options: He was not known for keeping a tidy lab.
In 1945, Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the Nobel Prize.
qs.why: not known for keeping a tidy lab = 他的實驗室向來不以整齊出名。
qs.evidence: He was not known for keeping a tidy lab.

qs.q: Statement: Fleming was able to produce large amounts of penicillin soon after his discovery.
qs.why: 第四段：他很難大量生產，大約十年沒什麼進展 → False。
qs.evidence: Fleming found it very difficult to produce penicillin in large amounts

qs.q: In paragraph 4, in "it could cure infections", what does "it" refer to?
qs.why: found a way to purify it and showed that it could cure infections——兩個 it 都指盤尼西林。
qs.evidence: found a way to purify it and showed that it could cure infections

qs.q: What is the writer's main point in the last paragraph?
options: Fleming did not deserve the Nobel Prize.
A lucky accident matters only when someone notices and understands it.
Most discoveries in medicine are accidents.
qs.why: 最後一句：an accident only matters if someone notices it and understands what it means。

title: Why Hospitals Want You to Report Mistakes
paras: In the past, many hospitals dealt with mistakes by looking for someone to blame. A nurse who gave the wrong dose might be punished, and everyone else would learn one lesson: if you make a mistake, keep quiet. As a result, many errors were never reported, and the same problems happened again and again.

Today, many hospitals try to build what is called a 'just culture'. The idea is that most errors are not caused by bad people but by bad systems: confusing labels, tired staff, unclear instructions. If a hospital only punishes individuals, it never fixes the system, and the next person falls into the same trap.

Consider a common type of case. Two medicines come in boxes that look almost the same. A nurse picks up the wrong box and notices just in time. If she had been punished for the near miss, she would probably have kept it to herself. Because she reported it, the pharmacy changed the way the boxes were stored, and other nurses were warned.

Aviation is often given as an example. Pilots are encouraged to report their own errors, and in some systems these reports are confidential. Many experts believe that this openness has helped make flying much safer than it used to be.

A just culture does not mean that nobody is ever responsible. Staff who take dangerous shortcuts on purpose can still face consequences. But the main question changes from 'Who did this?' to 'Why did this happen, and how can we stop it from happening again?'
zh: 過去很多醫院處理錯誤的方式是找人來怪：給錯劑量的護理師可能被懲罰，其他人學到的是「犯錯就閉嘴」，結果很多錯誤沒被通報，同樣的問題一再發生。現在很多醫院想建立「公正文化」：大部分錯誤不是壞人造成的，而是壞的系統——容易混淆的標籤、疲累的人員、不清楚的指示；只懲罰個人，系統永遠不會修好，下一個人又會掉進同樣的陷阱。例如兩種藥的盒子幾乎一樣，護理師拿錯了、及時發現；如果她因為這次跡近錯失被罰，大概就不會說出來；因為她通報了，藥局改了盒子的擺放方式，也提醒了其他護理師。航空業常被拿來當例子：鼓勵機師通報自己的錯誤，有些制度還會保密；很多專家認為這種開放讓飛行比以前安全得多。公正文化不代表沒有人要負責，故意走危險捷徑的人還是會有後果；但主要的問題從「是誰做的？」變成「為什麼會發生？怎麼避免再發生？」

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why many hospitals now encourage staff to report errors
How to store boxes of medicine
qs.why: 整篇在講從「找人來怪」轉成「公正文化」、鼓勵通報錯誤的原因。

qs.q: According to paragraph 2, what causes most errors?
qs.why: most errors are not caused by bad people but by bad systems。
qs.evidence: most errors are not caused by bad people but by bad systems

qs.q: What happened because the nurse in paragraph 3 reported the near miss?
options: The pharmacy changed how the boxes were stored.
The medicine was taken off the market.
qs.why: Because she reported it, the pharmacy changed the way the boxes were stored。
qs.evidence: the pharmacy changed the way the boxes were stored

qs.q: Statement: In a just culture, staff are never responsible for anything.
qs.why: 最後一段第一句就說公正文化不代表沒有人要負責 → False。
qs.evidence: A just culture does not mean that nobody is ever responsible.

qs.q: Statement: The idea of a just culture was first developed in Taiwan.
qs.why: 文章完全沒提公正文化從哪裡開始 → Not Given。

title: Letter to My Younger Self
paras: Dear Young Nurse, I am writing this after thirty years on the wards, and I wish someone had written a letter like this to me when I started. I was nervous, proud and very tired, and I made almost every mistake a new nurse can make. Here is what I have learned.

First, ask questions. In my first year, I pretended to understand things that I didn't, because I was afraid of looking stupid. Once, I wasn't sure how to set up a pump, and I should have asked my senior. Instead, I guessed. Luckily, she noticed in time. I wish I had understood earlier that good nurses ask; it is the dangerous ones who never do.

Second, look after your body. I used to lift patients without help because I wanted to finish quickly. Now, at fifty-four, I have back pain almost every day. If only I had used the lifting equipment and asked for a hand. Your back has to last your whole career.

Third, do not take everything home with you. Some days, you will lose a patient, or a family will shout at you, or you will feel that you did not do enough. I spent years replaying those days at night instead of sleeping. I should have talked to my colleagues more. Many of them were carrying the same feelings.

Finally, do not stop learning. I wish I were twenty-two again, with all the new things you will see: new treatments, new technology, new ways of caring. I don't regret becoming a nurse, not for one day. But I wish I had enjoyed the journey a little more and worried a little less. With love, An Old Nurse
zh: 一位做了三十年的護理師寫信給年輕護理師：她真希望當年有人寫這樣的信給她。第一，要發問：她第一年怕看起來很笨，不懂裝懂；有一次不確定怎麼裝輸液幫浦，應該問學姊卻自己猜，還好學姊及時發現。她希望自己早點明白，好護理師會發問，不問的才危險。第二，照顧身體：她以前為了快點做完，常常不找人幫忙就搬病人，現在五十四歲幾乎天天背痛——要是當初有用移位設備、請人幫忙就好了。第三，不要把所有事都帶回家：有些日子會失去病人、被家屬吼、覺得自己做得不夠；她好幾年晚上一直重播那些日子而睡不著，她應該多跟同事聊，很多人也背著同樣的感受。最後，不要停止學習：她真希望自己再回到二十二歲，看到新的治療、科技和照護方式。她從來不後悔當護理師，但希望當初多享受一點過程、少擔心一點。

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the letter?
options: To give advice to new nurses based on the writer's experience
To explain how to use lifting equipment
qs.why: 整封信是資深護理師用自己的遺憾給新人建議：發問、照顧身體、別把事情都帶回家、繼續學習。

qs.q: Why did the writer not ask questions in her first year?
options: She was afraid of looking stupid.
qs.why: 第二段：because I was afraid of looking stupid。
qs.evidence: because I was afraid of looking stupid

qs.q: Statement: The writer has back pain because she used to lift patients without help.
qs.why: used to lift… without help → 現在五十四歲天天背痛；If only I had used the lifting equipment 也表示她後悔 → True。
qs.evidence: I used to lift patients without help because I wanted to finish quickly.

qs.q: In paragraph 4, 'replaying those days' means…
options: thinking about those days again and again
qs.why: replay 本來是重播；她晚上不睡覺一直重播那些日子 = 一直反覆去想。
qs.evidence: I spent years replaying those days at night instead of sleeping.

qs.q: Statement: The writer regrets becoming a nurse.
qs.why: I don't regret becoming a nurse, not for one day → False。她後悔的是沒多享受過程。
qs.evidence: I don't regret becoming a nurse, not for one day.

title: Ask Dr. Lee: 'I Wish I Had Chosen a Different Major'
paras: Dear Dr. Lee, I am a second-year nursing student, and I think I made the wrong choice. My parents wanted me to study nursing because it is a stable job, and I agreed without really thinking about it. Now I find anatomy boring, and my first placement was exhausting. All my friends seem to love their majors. I wish I had studied design instead. Should I quit? Lost in Taichung

Dear Lost, first, thank you for being so honest. Many students feel exactly the way you do in their second year, but very few say it out loud. Feeling bored or tired does not necessarily mean you chose the wrong path. The second year is often the hardest: the subjects are difficult, and you have not yet seen the parts of the job that many nurses find most rewarding.

That said, your feelings deserve to be taken seriously. Before you make any big decision, try to find out more. Talk to nurses who work in different areas. A busy emergency room is very different from a school clinic or a research job. You might discover a side of nursing that suits you better than you imagined.

It is also worth asking what exactly you wish were different. If you wish you had more creative work, there may be ways to combine your interests. Some nurses design health education materials, and others work on hospital apps. On the other hand, if you are sure that you would be happier in another field, it is not too late to change. Many people switch careers, and the knowledge you have gained will not be wasted.

Whatever you decide, try not to make the decision only to please others, or only because of one bad month. You shouldn't have to live your parents' dream, but you also shouldn't throw away two years of work without looking carefully at your options. Dr. Lee
zh: 一位護理系二年級學生寫信給專欄：父母覺得護理是穩定的工作，她沒多想就答應了；現在覺得解剖學很無聊、第一次實習累壞了，朋友好像都很愛自己的科系，她真希望當初讀設計，問該不該休學。李醫師回信：謝謝她這麼誠實，很多二年級學生都有一樣的感覺，只是很少人說出口；覺得無聊或疲累不一定代表選錯路，二年級常是最難的一年，還沒看到這份工作最有成就感的部分。不過她的感受應該被認真對待：做重大決定前先多了解，去問不同領域的護理師——忙碌的急診和學校保健室、研究工作很不一樣。也值得問自己到底希望哪裡不同：如果想要更有創意的工作，有些護理師設計衛教教材，有些做醫院 App；如果確定在別的領域會更快樂，現在改也不嫌晚，學到的知識不會白費。不論怎麼決定，不要只為了讓別人開心，或只因為一個糟糕的月份就決定。

qs.q: Why did the student choose nursing?
options: Because her parents wanted her to and it is a stable job
Because her friends were studying nursing
qs.why: 第一段：My parents wanted me to study nursing because it is a stable job。
qs.evidence: My parents wanted me to study nursing because it is a stable job

qs.q: Statement: According to Dr. Lee, feeling bored always means you chose the wrong major.
qs.why: does not necessarily mean = 不一定代表；「一定代表選錯」跟原文相反 → False。
qs.evidence: Feeling bored or tired does not necessarily mean you chose the wrong path.

qs.q: What does Dr. Lee suggest the student do before deciding?
options: Talk to nurses who work in different areas
qs.why: 第三段：Talk to nurses who work in different areas。
qs.evidence: Talk to nurses who work in different areas

qs.q: In paragraph 4, in "others work on hospital apps", who are "others"?
qs.why: Some nurses design…, and others work on…——others = other nurses。
qs.evidence: Some nurses design health education materials, and others work on hospital apps.

qs.q: What is Dr. Lee's overall advice?
options: Stay in nursing no matter what.
Find out more and make the decision carefully, for herself.
qs.why: 她沒有叫學生留下或離開，而是先多了解、想清楚，不要只為了別人或一個壞月份決定。

title: What People Regret Most
paras: Everyone has regrets. Some are small, such as 'I shouldn't have eaten that second piece of cake', and some stay with us for years. Psychologists who study regret have found some interesting patterns in what people regret and when.

One finding is that the kind of regret seems to change over time. In the short term, people often regret things they did: an angry message they sent, money they spent, something they said in a meeting. Over the long term, however, people more often regret things they did not do. Looking back on their lives, many say things like 'I wish I had travelled more' or 'I wish I had told her how I felt.'

Why might this be? One explanation is that we usually take action to fix the results of our mistakes. If you send an unkind message, you can apologise. But a chance you never took stays open in your imagination. You can always wonder what might have happened, and the imagined result is often better than reality would have been.

Regret is not only negative. Researchers point out that it can help us learn. A student who thinks 'I should have started revising earlier' may plan better for the next exam. The problem comes when people replay the same regret again and again without changing anything.

For nurses, this is useful knowledge. Patients near the end of life sometimes talk about their regrets, and listening without judging can be an important part of care. And for students, the research offers a simple lesson: when you are not sure whether to try something new, remember that, years later, you may be more likely to regret not trying.
zh: 每個人都有遺憾，有些很小（「我不該吃第二塊蛋糕」），有些跟著我們好多年。研究遺憾的心理學家發現了一些模式：遺憾的種類似乎會隨時間改變——短期內，人常後悔「做了」的事，像傳出的氣話、花掉的錢、會議上說的話；長期來看，人比較常後悔「沒做」的事，回顧人生時常說「真希望我多去旅行」「真希望我有告訴她我的感受」。一種解釋是：做錯的事我們通常會採取行動補救，傳了不客氣的訊息可以道歉；但沒把握的機會會一直留在想像裡，你永遠可以猜想本來可能發生什麼，而想像的結果常比現實更好。遺憾不只是負面的，研究者指出它能幫助我們學習：想著「我應該早點開始複習」的學生，下次考試可能會計畫得更好；問題在於一再重播同樣的遺憾卻什麼都不改。對護理師來說，臨終病人有時會談起遺憾，不帶評判地傾聽是照護的重要部分；對學生來說，不確定要不要嘗試新事物時，記得多年後你可能更容易後悔「沒試」。

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Patterns in what people regret, and what we can learn from them
How to apologise after sending an angry message
Why travelling is good for your health
qs.why: 整篇講心理學家發現的遺憾模式（短期後悔做了、長期後悔沒做）、原因，以及對護理和學習的意義。

qs.q: In the short term, what do people often regret?
qs.why: In the short term, people often regret things they did；長期才比較後悔沒做的事。
qs.evidence: In the short term, people often regret things they did

qs.q: Which sentence explains why a missed chance can stay with us?
options: But a chance you never took stays open in your imagination.
qs.why: 沒把握的機會會一直留在想像裡（stays open in your imagination），所以一直放不下。
qs.evidence: But a chance you never took stays open in your imagination.

qs.q: Statement: Researchers say that regret can help people learn.
qs.why: Researchers point out that it can help us learn → True。
qs.evidence: Researchers point out that it can help us learn.

qs.q: Statement: Nurses should tell patients not to talk about their regrets.
qs.why: 文章說不帶評判地傾聽是照護的重要部分，跟「叫病人不要說」相反 → False。
qs.evidence: listening without judging can be an important part of care

title: Florence Nightingale, Who Counted the Dead
paras: Florence Nightingale, who is often called the founder of modern nursing, was born in 1820 in the Italian city of Florence, which gave her her name.
