Her family was wealthy, and her parents expected her to marry and live a comfortable life. Nightingale, however, believed that she had a calling to care for the sick.

In 1854, during the Crimean War, she travelled with a group of nurses to a British army hospital in Scutari, which is now part of Istanbul. Conditions there were terrible. The wards, where wounded soldiers lay close together, were dirty and crowded, and there were rats everywhere. Far more soldiers were dying from diseases such as cholera and typhus than from their wounds.

Nightingale and her nurses cleaned the wards, washed the soldiers' clothes and organised proper meals. At night, she walked through the wards carrying a lamp, which is why soldiers called her 'the Lady with the Lamp'. After a government commission improved the drains and the water supply, the death rate at the hospital fell sharply.

What is less well known is that Nightingale was also a gifted statistician. She kept careful records of how many soldiers died and why. She then presented the data in colourful diagrams, which made the message clear even to people who did not like numbers: most of the deaths could have been prevented. Her work helped to persuade the government to improve conditions in army hospitals. She later became the first woman to be elected a member of the Royal Statistical Society.

In 1860, Nightingale opened a training school for nurses at St Thomas' Hospital in London, which helped to turn nursing into a respected profession. She died in 1910. Today, International Nurses Day is celebrated on 12 May, which was her birthday.
zh: 南丁格爾常被稱為現代護理的創始人，1820 年生於義大利佛羅倫斯，名字就來自這座城市。她家境富裕，父母期待她結婚、過舒適的生活，但她相信照顧病人是她的使命。1854 年克里米亞戰爭期間，她帶著一群護士到斯庫塔里（今伊斯坦堡的一部分）的英軍醫院：環境很糟，傷兵擠在骯髒的病房裡，到處是老鼠，死於霍亂、斑疹傷寒等疾病的士兵遠比死於傷口的多。她們清潔病房、洗衣服、安排正常的餐點；她晚上提著燈巡視病房，所以士兵叫她「提燈天使」。政府派來的委員會改善排水和供水後，醫院的死亡率大幅下降。比較少人知道的是，她也是很有天分的統計學家：她仔細記錄士兵死亡的人數和原因，再畫成彩色圖表，讓不喜歡數字的人也看得懂——大部分死亡本來可以避免。她的工作說服政府改善軍醫院，她後來也成為第一位當選皇家統計學會會員的女性。1860 年她在倫敦聖湯瑪士醫院創辦護理學校，幫助護理成為受尊重的專業。她 1910 年過世；今天的國際護師節是 5 月 12 日，就是她的生日。

qs.q: Why was Florence Nightingale called 'the Lady with the Lamp'?
options: She invented a new kind of lamp.
She walked through the wards at night carrying a lamp.
She lit the lamps in the streets of London.
qs.why: 第三段：At night, she walked through the wards carrying a lamp, which is why…——which 指前面整件事。
qs.evidence: At night, she walked through the wards carrying a lamp

qs.q: Statement: More soldiers in the hospital died from disease than from their wounds.
qs.why: Far more soldiers were dying from diseases… than from their wounds → True。
qs.evidence: Far more soldiers were dying from diseases such as cholera and typhus than from their wounds.

qs.q: What did her diagrams show?
options: That most of the deaths could have been prevented
That the war was almost over
qs.why: 冒號後面就是圖表要傳達的訊息：most of the deaths could have been prevented。
qs.evidence: most of the deaths could have been prevented

qs.q: In paragraph 1, in "which gave her her name", what does "which" refer to?
qs.why: 逗號前面就是 the Italian city of Florence；非限定的 which 補充說明這座城市。
qs.evidence: the Italian city of Florence, which gave her her name

qs.q: Statement: Nightingale wrote several books about statistics.
qs.why: 文章說她做紀錄、畫圖表、當選統計學會會員，沒提她寫過統計學的書 → Not Given。

title: Welcome to Sunrise Hospital
paras: Welcome to Sunrise Hospital, which has served the people of southern Taiwan since 1978. This short guide will help you find your way around during your first visit.

The main entrance is on Harbor Road, where you will also find the bus stop and the taxi rank. As you come in, you will see the information desk, which is open from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. The volunteers there, most of whom are retired teachers and nurses, can answer questions in Mandarin, Taiwanese and English.

The outpatient clinics are on the first and second floors. Our emergency department, which is open 24 hours a day, has its own entrance at the back of the building. Please do not use the main entrance in an emergency, because it is further from the treatment rooms.

On the third floor is the children's ward, whose walls were painted by local art students. Next to it is the family room, where parents can rest, make tea and take a shower. The rooftop garden, which was opened in 2019, is a quiet place for patients and visitors to get some fresh air. It is closed when it rains.

Visiting hours are from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. In the intensive care unit, where patients need extra rest, only two visitors are allowed at a time. If you have any questions, please ask any member of staff, all of whom wear blue name badges.
zh: 歡迎來到朝陽醫院，1978 年起服務南台灣。這份簡介幫你第一次來時找到路：正門在港口路，公車站和計程車招呼站也在那裡；進門會看到服務台，早上七點到晚上九點開放，那裡的志工大多是退休老師和護理師，可以用國語、台語和英語回答問題。門診在一、二樓；急診 24 小時開放，入口在大樓後面，緊急狀況請不要走正門，因為離治療室比較遠。三樓是兒科病房，牆壁是在地美術系學生畫的；旁邊是家屬休息室，家長可以休息、泡茶、洗澡。屋頂花園 2019 年啟用，是病人和訪客呼吸新鮮空氣的安靜地方，下雨時關閉。探病時間是上午十一點到晚上八點；加護病房的病人需要多休息，一次只能兩位訪客。有問題可以問任何工作人員，他們都戴藍色名牌。

qs.q: What is the purpose of this text?
options: To help visitors find their way around the hospital
To advertise jobs at the hospital
To explain the history of southern Taiwan
qs.why: 第一段：This short guide will help you find your way around，後面一層一層介紹位置和規定。

qs.q: Who are most of the volunteers at the information desk?
options: Students from a local art school
qs.why: most of whom are retired teachers and nurses：whom 指前面的 volunteers。
qs.evidence: most of whom are retired teachers and nurses

qs.q: Why should people not use the main entrance in an emergency?
options: It is further from the treatment rooms.
qs.why: 第三段最後：because it is further from the treatment rooms。
qs.evidence: because it is further from the treatment rooms

qs.q: Statement: The rooftop garden is open in all weather.
qs.why: It is closed when it rains：下雨會關，不是任何天氣都開 → False。
qs.evidence: It is closed when it rains.

qs.q: Statement: Children are allowed to visit patients in the intensive care unit.
qs.why: 只說加護病房一次限兩位訪客，沒說小孩能不能進去 → Not Given。

title: Virginia Apgar and the Ten-Point Score
paras: One minute after birth, almost every baby born in a modern hospital is given its first test. The test, which takes only a few seconds, is called the Apgar score. It was named after Virginia Apgar, an American doctor whose simple idea has helped to save a great many newborn lives.

Apgar, who was born in 1909, originally wanted to be a surgeon. However, she was advised to choose anaesthesia instead, a field in which few doctors worked at the time. She went on to become a leading anaesthesiologist in New York, where she worked closely with mothers giving birth.

In the early 1950s, Apgar noticed a problem. Doctors and nurses had no quick, standard way to decide whether a newborn baby needed help. Babies who were having trouble breathing were sometimes not noticed until it was too late. In 1952 she proposed a simple scoring system, which she published the following year.

The score looks at five signs: the baby's skin colour, heart rate, reflexes, muscle tone and breathing. Each sign is given 0, 1 or 2 points, so the total is between 0 and 10. The test is done at one minute and again at five minutes after birth. A low score tells the team, quickly and clearly, that the baby may need help, such as support with breathing.

Later, the five signs were turned into a memory aid that uses the letters of her name: Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity and Respiration. Apgar, who later worked on preventing birth defects, died in 1974. Her score, which is still used around the world, remains one of the simplest and most useful tools in medicine.
zh: 在現代醫院出生的嬰兒，出生一分鐘時幾乎都會做第一個檢查：只要幾秒鐘的亞培格評分。它以美國醫師維吉妮亞．亞培格命名，她的簡單點子救了很多新生兒。她 1909 年出生，原本想當外科醫師，卻被建議改走麻醉——當時很少醫師投入的領域；後來她成為紐約頂尖的麻醉科醫師，和生產中的媽媽密切合作。1950 年代初她發現一個問題：醫護人員沒有快速、標準的方法判斷新生兒需不需要幫助，有呼吸困難的嬰兒有時太晚才被發現。1952 年她提出簡單的評分系統，隔年發表。評分看五個徵象：膚色、心跳、反射、肌肉張力和呼吸，每項 0、1 或 2 分，總分 0 到 10；在出生後一分鐘和五分鐘各做一次，分數低就清楚快速地告訴團隊寶寶可能需要幫助，例如呼吸支持。後來這五項被做成用她名字字母的口訣：Appearance、Pulse、Grimace、Activity、Respiration。她後來投入預防出生缺陷，1974 年過世；她的評分至今仍在全世界使用。

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a doctor created a quick test for newborn babies
qs.why: 整篇在講亞培格評分怎麼來的、怎麼做、為什麼重要。

qs.q: What problem did Apgar notice?
options: There was no quick, standard way to check whether a newborn needed help.
There were not enough surgeons in New York.
qs.why: 第三段：Doctors and nurses had no quick, standard way to decide whether a newborn baby needed help。
qs.evidence: Doctors and nurses had no quick, standard way to decide whether a newborn baby needed help.

qs.q: When is the Apgar test done?
options: Only at one minute after birth
At one minute and again at five minutes after birth
Once a day for the first week
qs.why: The test is done at one minute and again at five minutes after birth。
qs.evidence: The test is done at one minute and again at five minutes after birth.

qs.q: Statement: The highest possible Apgar score is 10.
qs.why: 五項各 0–2 分，so the total is between 0 and 10 → 最高 10 分，True。
qs.evidence: so the total is between 0 and 10

qs.q: Statement: The Apgar score is no longer used today.
qs.why: Her score, which is still used around the world——現在全世界還在用 → False。
qs.evidence: Her score, which is still used around the world
